text:
Alice: quick heads-up — ran side-by-side: synthetic wrk-based load vs our replay harness (recorded client traffic) for the kv-heavy chat benchmark. numbers diverge badly.
Brad: how badly? p95/p99?
Alice: p95 wrk=110ms, p95 replay=240ms, p99 wrk=320ms, p99 replay=780ms. throughput similar.
Carla: wow that's huge. are you using same qps, seq len, and concurrency?
Alice: yes — same request trace. wrk script used keepalive connections pooled across threads. our replay opens new connections per request by default (old config).
Devon: that alone can explain TLS+TCP handoff overhead. did you check connection reuse stats?
Alice: yep. replay logs show ~60% of requests did full TLS handshake because pool size small. changed pool to reuse channels -> p95 dropped to 130ms.
Brad: so synthetic bench was optimistic because it kept TLS/TCP warm. classic.
Carla: also watch Nagle/TCP_NODELAY — some clients batch small writes. are we enabling NODELAY?
Alice: good catch. wrk sets TCP_NODELAY by default on the socket lib we used. our python replay client didn't. toggling NODELAY shaved ~8-12ms on tail.
Devon: grpc vs rest comparison? we saw grpc channels amortize handshake and TLS, but misconfigured max_parallel_streams can bottleneck.
Alice: for gRPC: if channel count < req concurrency you get head-of-line. replay initially had one channel per thread, which was fine, but our default client created a new channel per request in a codepath. not good.
Carla: aside from transport, any runtime-side surprises? kernel selection/ batching?
Alice: yes — profiling showed runtime picked float16-fused-kernel for certain seq_len but for batch sizes >8 it fell back to slower kernel due to workspace allocation heuristics. that triggered a perf cliff under replay's bursty pattern.
Brad: can you paste profile snippet?
Alice: ```
nvprof output:
Time(%)  Calls  Avg  Min  Max  Name
45.2    120    3.2ms 1.1ms  12.6ms  attention_fused_fp16
30.1    30     9.5ms 8.8ms  10.2ms  attention_unfused_fp16
12.7    400    0.8ms 0.1ms  2.4ms   cudaMemcpyAsync
```
Carla: so workspace heuristic causes fallback to unfused kernel. any env toggles?
Alice: we have a kernel selector table based on (seq_len, batch, model_variant). selector had a bug: >=8 was treated as large batch. patched locally to threshold 16 and retested -> fused kernel used more often, p95 improved ~25ms.
Devon: KV cache behavior? replay vs synthetic might stress cache differently.
Alice: yes — replay opens many ephemeral sessions and doesn't reuse cached prefixes, which increases KV cache churn. cache eviction thrashed, causing extra memory copies and re-encoding. observed spike in GC-like pauses in worker process.
Brad: do we have metrics for kv-hit-rate per-run?
Alice: added a quick counter: wrk-run kv_hit=0.82, replay kv_hit=0.45. that correlates with extra 40-120ms per request when cache cold.
Carla: actionables?
Alice: 1) Update replay harness to default to connection reuse and NODELAY. 2) Add option to replay that preserves session stickiness to mimic production clients. 3) Adjust kernel selector threshold and add telemetry for chosen kernel per-request. 4) Expose kv-hit-rate in benchmark dashboard.
Devon: also add a standard apples-to-apples checklist in perf playbook: transport settings (KEEPALIVE, NODELAY), channel pooling, TLS resumption, and client concurrency semantics.
infra-bot: benchmark-run recorded: id=br-20260303-11, artifacts=/runs/br-20260303-11/*.tgz
Brad: perfect. can someone file a small RFC for the replay harness defaults? Carla/Devon?
Carla: I'll draft it today, include reproduction steps and the before/after numbers.
Alice: dropping the local patch to kernel selector in the PR as well, with flags to toggle.
Devon: i'll add kv-hit-rate graphs to console and a synthetic option to force cold-cache runs.
Brad: nice. learning: synthetic tools are fine but watch transport/connection semantics and cache patterns. otherwise you end up optimizing for the harness, not prod. :100:
Alice: yep — and we should standardize a minimal benchmark config that everyone runs for comparisons.
Carla: +1. I'll add to perf playbook and ping infra to schedule nightly replay runs with both configs.
Alice: thanks all. leaving logs & profile links in the PR.
